messages:
samir: heads up — saw a 3x IOPS spike across eu-west2 gnode pools at ~03:10 UTC during the nightly scrub window, causing ~60% ephemeral eviction and blocking ~40% of GPU allocations
eng-infra-bot: alert: scrub-job-runner started scrub on nodes gnode-*-eu2 at 03:05 (job id: scrub-2026-03-18-03)
maya: ack, saw a flood of IO wait in the metrics. provisioning queues backed up and a couple of batch jobs failed to get GPUs.
juan: any chance scrub got a higher priority IO class? we recently bumped systemd slice configs for fs maintenance on some hosts.
samir: good call — looks like `ionice -c2 -n0` ended up on the scrub process after the maintenance PR last month. scrub was already parallelized across 16 workers.
lina: ouch. that + parallel workers explains the headroom collapse. can we throttle the scrub?
maya: quick mitigation: switch scrub to `ionice -c3 -n7` and reduce workers from 16 -> 4, and ramp with sleep between jobs. will that buy us time?
oncall: can we flip that in eu-west2 now? we still have inflight provisioning backlog.
juan: do we have a flag in the scrub service to tune concurrency remotely? I can roll a config change with zero restart.
eng-infra-bot: deploy plan created by juan: scrub-config-rate-limit v1 -> canary on 10 nodes, then 50, then 100 (stagger 2m).
samir: canary seems right. also let's gate scrubs on GPU provisioning pressure: if GPU queue_len > 10 for >2m, pause scrubs.
lina: agree. we can add a simple check to the controller: `if gpu_queue_len > 10: pause` — easy to add to scrub-runner.
maya: FYI cost note — nightly scrubs doing full-device reads on 20k nodes adds to egress/billing and increases wear. reducing workers saves both cost and wear.
juan: rolling canary now — applying ionice + worker cap to 10 nodes as stage1. monitoring dashboards hooked.
eng-infra-bot: canary applied to scrub-config-rate-limit on nodes: gnode-eu2-{12..21}
oncall: seeing IOPS tail drop on canary nodes, allocation failures dropping in eu-west2 backlog. nice work. :thumbsup:
samir: let's schedule a follow-up to rework scrub cadence: move heavy scrubs to weekly deep checks and daily light checks, and add an adaptive backoff based on `gpu_queue_len`. owner: lina.
lina: will create an RFC for scrub orchestration and a follow-up ticket to implement adaptive backoff. ETA EOD tomorrow.
maya: also propose instrumenting per-node wear counters (SMART host-level) in the scrub job so we de-prioritize drives approaching wear thresholds.
juan: noted. opening ticket for SMART sampling and eviction hints.
eng-infra-bot: incident closed: scrub-induced provisioning-impact (post-mitigation) — severity: low, root cause: high-scrub-io-priority + high concurrency, mitigation: ionice downgrade + concurrency cap + canary rollout.
samir: thanks all. after RFC we should run a 2-week test with new cadence before full rollout.
